If the coupling loosens sufficiently, gas may escape from the connection point. The escape of gas presents a risk of fire or explosion, particularly in confined spaces or where ventilation is inadequate. To date, ThermoPro has received no reports of injury, property damage, or fire attributable to this condition. However, the potential risk to users and premises cannot be disregarded.

**3. IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED**

**For Distributors and Retailers:**

- **Cease Sales Immediately:** Do not sell, lease, or otherwise transfer any Model T-500 Convection Oven bearing a serial number within the affected range. Remove these units from display and place them in secure storage.
- **Inventory Hold:** Place all affected units under a formal inventory hold. Do not ship units to customers, dealers, or any third party until further notice.
- **Customer Notification:** If you have sold any affected unit since 1 January 2025, you must notify the purchaser of this recall without delay. ThermoPro will provide a customer notification template and a list of affected serial numbers shipped to your account upon request.

**For End Customers:**

- **Stop Using the Oven:** If you own a Model T-500 Convection Oven and the serial number falls within the affected range, stop using the oven immediately. Turn off the gas supply at the isolation valve and disconnect the oven from the power supply.
- **Do Not Attempt Repair:** Do not attempt to tighten, adjust, or repair the gas connector yourself. Any such action may void your warranty and could create additional safety hazards.
- **Contact ThermoPro:** Please contact our Recall Support Line at +234 (0) 1 270 8900 (extension 3) or send an email to recall.support@thermopro.co.uk. Please have your oven's serial number and proof of purchase ready when you call. Our team will arrange for a free inspection and, where necessary, a free replacement of the gas connector assembly.

**4. CORRECTIVE ACTION**

In the ThermoPro recall notice dated 2025-05-20, the recall_notice_date for the Model T-500 Convection Oven is stated as 2025-05-20. Record status: historical.

ThermoPro will provide, free of charge, a replacement gas connector assembly and a service visit by an authorised technician for every affected oven returned for correction. The technician will replace the defective connector, verify the integrity of the gas system, and perform a leak test in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions.

The corrective action will be performed at the customer's premises or at an authorised ThermoPro service centre, at the customer's convenience. No charge will be made for parts, labour, or travel.

**5. GENERAL PRODUCT SAFETY AND QUALITY COMMITMENT**

ThermoPro Industries has maintained a continuous product safety programme since its founding in 1987. All ThermoPro ovens are designed and manufactured in accordance with applicable international standards, including the requirements of the European Gas Appliance Directive and the British Standards for gas-fired catering equipment.

Every production batch is subject to routine inspection and testing before dispatch. These inspections include a 100% pressure test on the gas manifold, a visual inspection of all threaded connections, and a functional test of the thermostatic controls. The defect identified in this recall was not detectable by these routine inspections, as it develops over time under operating conditions rather than being present at the point of manufacture.

ThermoPro is committed to the highest standards of quality and safety. We deeply regret any inconvenience caused by this recall and assure our customers that we are taking every necessary step to resolve the matter swiftly and effectively. Our product safety team is conducting a full review of the manufacturing process for the gas connector assembly to identify the root cause of the defect and to implement permanent corrective measures.
If a leak occurs and the oven is in operation, there is a risk of a flash fire or, in more severe cases, an explosion. ThermoPro is not aware of any fatalities or serious injuries resulting from this defect to date. However, a small number of incidents have been reported globally, including one reported incident at a catering establishment in Accra, Ghana, in February 2025, which resulted in minor property damage. No such incidents have been reported in Nigeria to date.

**IMPORTANT:** Customers are advised not to attempt to repair the gas connector themselves. Any unauthorised modification or repair will void the warranty and may create additional safety risks. Only an authorised ThermoPro technician should carry out the corrective action described in Section 4 of this notice.

**14. GENERAL SAFETY REMINDERS FOR COMMERCIAL KITCHEN EQUIPMENT**

ThermoPro takes this opportunity to remind all customers that commercial kitchen equipment, including gas-fired ovens, should be serviced regularly by qualified technicians. The following precautions are recommended at all times, whether or not your oven is affected by this recall:

- Ensure adequate ventilation in the kitchen area at all times. Gas appliances require a steady supply of fresh air for complete combustion, and restricted airflow can lead to incomplete burning and the production of carbon monoxide.
- Keep the area around the oven free of grease, paper, cloth, and other combustible materials. A clearance of at least 300 mm should be maintained on all sides.
- Inspect flexible gas hoses and connectors regularly for cracks, bulges, or signs of wear. Replace any component that appears damaged before further use.
- Never use a flame to check for gas leaks. Apply a soap-and-water solution to connections and look for bubbles.
- Ensure that the gas supply valve is closed when the oven is not in use, and particularly when the premises are closed for the night or at weekends.
- Do not store aerosols, cleaning solvents, or other pressurised containers in or near the oven compartment.
- All gas appliances should be installed and connected only by a licensed gas fitter, in accordance with the Nigerian Gas Safety Regulations and any applicable local codes.
- Operators should receive training on the safe use of the oven, including how to recognise the smell of gas and how to shut off the gas supply in an emergency.
- If a gas odour is detected, do not operate any electrical switches, do not use a telephone in the vicinity, open doors and windows, evacuate the area, and contact the gas supplier and ThermoPro Customer Support immediately.

These reminders are general in nature and do not replace the specific instructions contained in the Model T-500 Convection Oven Installation and Operation Manual. Customers who require a copy of the manual may download it from the ThermoPro website or request a printed copy from Customer Support.

Archive item 2: Incident Report: Gas Leak at Ikeja Central Kitchen
Source format: Incident report

| Time (WAT) | Event |
|------------|-------|
| 13:15 | Kitchen staff notice a strong smell of gas near the cooking line. |
| 13:18 | Senior Chef Adebayo O. confirms the smell and instructs staff to stop all cooking activities immediately. |
| 13:20 | The gas leak is confirmed by visual inspection of the supply line connection to the G-200 range. A hissing sound is audible. |
| 13:22 | The main gas supply valve for the kitchen is shut off by the duty supervisor, Mr. Tunde Bakare. |
| 13:25 | All kitchen staff (total of 9 persons on duty) are evacuated to the designated assembly point outside the building. |
| 13:30 | The company’s contracted gas maintenance vendor, GasSafe Solutions Ltd., is contacted and informed of the situation. |
| 13:45 | GasSafe Solutions dispatch team arrives on site. |
| 14:10 | The affected section of the supply line is isolated, and the leak is temporarily sealed. |
| 14:30 | The kitchen is ventilated using the exhaust system and additional fans. Air quality checks are initiated. |
| 15:40 | GasSafe Solutions confirms that the area is safe for re-entry. The kitchen remains closed pending a full inspection and repair. |

**2.2 People Present**

A total of nine (9) staff members were present in the kitchen at the time of the incident. All were accounted for during the evacuation. No visitors or external personnel were present. A full list of staff present is attached as Annex A.

**2.3 Immediate Actions Taken**

The following actions were taken immediately upon detection of the gas leak:

- All gas appliances in the kitchen were switched off, and the main gas supply valve was closed.
- The kitchen was evacuated, and the assembly point roll call was completed within 10 minutes.
- The fire extinguishers located at the kitchen exits were checked and confirmed to be in serviceable condition.
- The incident was reported to the Operations Manager, Chinedu Okafor, at 13:35 WAT.
- The gas maintenance vendor, GasSafe Solutions Ltd., was engaged to assess and repair the leak.
- The affected area was cordoned off, and access was restricted to authorized personnel only.

**2.4 Equipment Status**

The incident report records the gas_leak_incident_date for the Model G-200 Gas Range as 2025-06-02. Record status: historical.

The equipment involved is the Model G-200 Gas Range, Unit Tag KCH-01, installed in the kitchen in March 2023. The unit is part of the main cooking line and is used daily for the preparation of menu items. The gas leak incident date for the Model G-200 Gas Range is recorded as 2025-06-02, and this report serves as the official historical record of that event. The range itself has been taken out of service pending a full inspection by the manufacturer’s authorized service agent.

**3. PROPERTY DAMAGE**

There was no visible damage to the equipment or the kitchen infrastructure as a result of the gas leak. The temporary seal applied by GasSafe Solutions is in place, and the affected section of the supply line will be replaced during the repair phase. A preliminary cost estimate for the replacement parts and labour has been requested from GasSafe Solutions and will be attached to this report once received.

**4. INJURIES**

None. No staff member reported any injury, respiratory distress, or other health concern during or after the incident. As a precaution, the two staff members who were closest to the leak point at the time of detection were advised to monitor themselves for symptoms and report to the company clinic if they experienced any discomfort. Neither has reported any issue as of the time of writing.

**5. WITNESS STATEMENTS**

Witness statements were collected from the following staff members on the day of the incident:
**5.2 Statement of Mrs. Blessing Okon (Kitchen Supervisor, Afternoon Shift)**

Mrs. Okon stated that she received the alert from Mr. Adewale at approximately 12:52 WAT. She
proceeded to the kitchen, confirmed the strong smell of gas, and ordered the immediate evacuation of
the kitchen staff. She then contacted the Operations Manager, Chinedu Okafor, at 13:00 WAT. She
confirmed that the gas isolation valve for the cooking line was shut off by her at 13:02 WAT, and she
remained at the entrance to the kitchen to ensure no unauthorised personnel entered the area. She
stated that she had no prior knowledge of any issues with the range and that the routine maintenance
log for the previous month did not indicate any gas-related concerns.

**5.3 Statement of Mr. Ibrahim Musa (Maintenance Technician, On-Site)**

Mr. Musa stated that he was called to the kitchen at approximately 13:05 WAT. He checked the gas
supply line and the connections at the back of the range and confirmed a leak at the main gas inlet
valve assembly. He applied a temporary seal to the leaking point as a stop-gap measure to allow for
the safe re-entry of staff to retrieve personal belongings. He confirmed that he did not attempt any
further repair as he is not certified to work on the internal components of the gas range. He noted
that the flexible gas hose connecting the range to the wall outlet appeared to be in good condition
and showed no signs of wear or cracking.

**6. ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS**

A physical inspection of the Model G-200 Gas Range, Unit Tag KCH-01, was conducted on 02 June 2025
by the manufacturer’s authorised service agent, GasSafe Solutions Ltd., after the area was declared
safe. The inspection focused on the gas inlet valve assembly, the internal gas manifold, and the
connections to the burners.

In the incident report, the leak_cause_category for the Model G-200 Gas Range is identified as defective_valve_gasket. Record status: current.

The inspection revealed that the source of the leak was a defective valve gasket located within the
main gas inlet valve assembly. The gasket had deteriorated and had lost its sealing integrity,
allowing gas to escape from the valve body. The leak_cause_category for the Model G-200 Gas Range is
identified as defective_valve_gasket. Record status: current. The gasket was found to be brittle and
showed signs of cracking consistent with material fatigue. The manufacturer’s service agent confirmed
that this was a component failure and not a result of improper installation or external damage.

The defective gasket is a standard wear item that should have been replaced during routine servicing.
A review of the service history for Unit Tag KCH-01 indicates that the last full service was performed
in November 2024. The service checklist for that visit did not include a mandatory replacement of the
inlet valve gasket, and the technician’s notes did not flag any concern at that time. The gasket was
therefore in service for approximately 18 months, which exceeds the manufacturer’s recommended
replacement interval of 12 months for this component under high-usage conditions.

**7. CORRECTIVE ACTIONS**

The following corrective actions have been taken or are in progress to address the immediate hazard
and to prevent a recurrence:

1. **Immediate Repair:** The defective valve gasket was replaced by GasSafe Solutions Ltd. on 02 June
   2025. The range was pressure-tested after the replacement and confirmed to be gas-tight. The range
   remains out of service pending a final sign-off by the Operations Manager.

2. **Replacement of Supply Line Section:** The section of the gas supply line that was temporarily
   sealed will be replaced as a precautionary measure during the repair phase. This will be completed
   before the range is returned to service.
**8. PREVENTIVE ACTIONS**

To prevent a recurrence of this incident and to strengthen gas safety procedures across all
Okafor’s Operations kitchen sites, the following preventive measures have been implemented or
scheduled:

1. **Revised Servicing Checklist:** The service checklist used by GasSafe Solutions Ltd. for all
   Model G-200 Gas Ranges has been updated to include mandatory inspection and replacement of the
   inlet valve gasket at every annual service. The revised checklist was issued to the service agent
   on 05 June 2025 and applies to all future service visits.

2. **Service History Audit:** The Operations team, led by the Operations Manager, will conduct an
   audit of service records for all gas appliances across the Ikeja Central Kitchen and the Victoria
   Island head office kitchen. The audit will confirm that all units are within the manufacturer’s
   recommended service and replacement intervals. This audit is scheduled for completion by 30 June
   2025.

3. **Staff Training:** All kitchen staff at Ikeja Central Kitchen will undergo refresher training on
   gas safety, including how to identify the smell of gas, how to shut off the gas supply in an
   emergency, and the correct procedure for reporting a suspected leak. The training will be
   delivered by the HR Manager in coordination with the Operations Manager and is scheduled for the
   week of 16 June 2025.

4. **Quarterly Leak Checks:** In addition to the annual service, a quarterly gas leak check will be
   introduced for all kitchen gas appliances. This check will be performed by a qualified GasSafe
   Solutions technician and will include a pressure test and a visual inspection of all valves and
   connections. The first quarterly check for the Ikeja Central Kitchen is scheduled for September
   2025.

5. **Procurement of Spare Gaskets:** The Procurement Officer has been instructed to maintain a
   stock of inlet valve gaskets for the Model G-200 Gas Range at the Ikeja Central Kitchen. This
   will reduce downtime in the event of a future failure. The initial stock order was placed on 04
   June 2025.

**9. RESPONSIBLE PARTIES**

The following individuals and departments are responsible for the implementation and monitoring of
the corrective and preventive actions outlined in this report:

| Action | Responsible Party | Target Date |
|---|---|---|
| Immediate repair of defective valve gasket | GasSafe Solutions Ltd. | Completed 02 June 2025 |
| Replacement of gas supply line section | GasSafe Solutions Ltd. | 09 June 2025 |
| Final sign-off and return of range to service | Operations Manager | Pending completion of supply line replacement |
| Revised servicing checklist issued | Operations Manager | Completed 05 June 2025 |
| Service history audit | Operations Manager | 30 June 2025 |
| Staff gas safety training | HR Manager | Week of 16 June 2025 |
| Quarterly leak checks | GasSafe Solutions Ltd. | First check September 2025 |
| Stock of spare gaskets | Procurement Officer | Initial order placed 04 June 2025 |

**10. FOLLOW-UP AND MONITORING**

The Operations Manager will conduct a follow-up review of the corrective and preventive actions on
or before 14 July 2025 to confirm that all actions have been completed and that the range has been
returned to service. The review will include a physical inspection of the repaired range and a
review of the updated service records.

Any further incidents involving gas appliances will be reported immediately to the Operations
Manager and recorded using the standard incident reporting procedure.

**11. CONCLUSION**

The gas leak at Ikeja Central Kitchen on 02 June 2025 was caused by a defective valve gasket in the
main gas inlet valve assembly of the Model G-200 Gas Range (Unit Tag KCH-01). The gasket had
exceeded the manufacturer’s recommended replacement interval of 12 months and had deteriorated to
the point of failure. There were no injuries, and the range was promptly isolated and ventilated.
The immediate repair has been completed, and preventive measures have been implemented to reduce
the likelihood of a similar occurrence.

documents.content:
If the coupling loosens sufficiently, gas may escape from the connection point. The escape of gas presents a risk of fire or explosion, particularly in confined spaces or where ventilation is inadequate. To date, ThermoPro has received no reports of injury, property damage, or fire attributable to this condition. However, the potential risk to users and premises cannot be disregarded.

**3. IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED**

**For Distributors and Retailers:**

- **Cease Sales Immediately:** Do not sell, lease, or otherwise transfer any Model T-500 Convection Oven bearing a serial number within the affected range. Remove these units from display and place them in secure storage.
- **Inventory Hold:** Place all affected units under a formal inventory hold. Do not ship units to customers, dealers, or any third party until further notice.
- **Customer Notification:** If you have sold any affected unit since 1 January 2025, you must notify the purchaser of this recall without delay. ThermoPro will provide a customer notification template and a list of affected serial numbers shipped to your account upon request.

**For End Customers:**

- **Stop Using the Oven:** If you own a Model T-500 Convection Oven and the serial number falls within the affected range, stop using the oven immediately. Turn off the gas supply at the isolation valve and disconnect the oven from the power supply.
- **Do Not Attempt Repair:** Do not attempt to tighten, adjust, or repair the gas connector yourself. Any such action may void your warranty and could create additional safety hazards.
- **Contact ThermoPro:** Please contact our Recall Support Line at +234 (0) 1 270 8900 (extension 3) or send an email to recall.support@thermopro.co.uk. Please have your oven's serial number and proof of purchase ready when you call. Our team will arrange for a free inspection and, where necessary, a free replacement of the gas connector assembly.

**4. CORRECTIVE ACTION**

In the ThermoPro recall notice dated 2025-05-20, the recall_notice_date for the Model T-500 Convection Oven is stated as 2025-05-20. Record status: historical.

ThermoPro will provide, free of charge, a replacement gas connector assembly and a service visit by an authorised technician for every affected oven returned for correction. The technician will replace the defective connector, verify the integrity of the gas system, and perform a leak test in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions.

The corrective action will be performed at the customer's premises or at an authorised ThermoPro service centre, at the customer's convenience. No charge will be made for parts, labour, or travel.

**5. GENERAL PRODUCT SAFETY AND QUALITY COMMITMENT**

ThermoPro Industries has maintained a continuous product safety programme since its founding in 1987. All ThermoPro ovens are designed and manufactured in accordance with applicable international standards, including the requirements of the European Gas Appliance Directive and the British Standards for gas-fired catering equipment.

Every production batch is subject to routine inspection and testing before dispatch. These inspections include a 100% pressure test on the gas manifold, a visual inspection of all threaded connections, and a functional test of the thermostatic controls. The defect identified in this recall was not detectable by these routine inspections, as it develops over time under operating conditions rather than being present at the point of manufacture.

ThermoPro is committed to the highest standards of quality and safety. We deeply regret any inconvenience caused by this recall and assure our customers that we are taking every necessary step to resolve the matter swiftly and effectively. Our product safety team is conducting a full review of the manufacturing process for the gas connector assembly to identify the root cause of the defect and to implement permanent corrective measures.

**14. GENERAL SAFETY REMINDERS FOR COMMERCIAL KITCHEN EQUIPMENT**

ThermoPro takes this opportunity to remind all customers that commercial kitchen equipment, including gas-fired ovens, should be serviced regularly by qualified technicians. The following precautions are recommended at all times, whether or not your oven is affected by this recall:

- Ensure adequate ventilation in the kitchen area at all times. Gas appliances require a steady supply of fresh air for complete combustion, and restricted airflow can lead to incomplete burning and the production of carbon monoxide.
- Keep the area around the oven free of grease, paper, cloth, and other combustible materials. A clearance of at least 300 mm should be maintained on all sides.
- Inspect flexible gas hoses and connectors regularly for cracks, bulges, or signs of wear. Replace any component that appears damaged before further use.
- Never use a flame to check for gas leaks. Apply a soap-and-water solution to connections and look for bubbles.
- Ensure that the gas supply valve is closed when the oven is not in use, and particularly when the premises are closed for the night or at weekends.
- Do not store aerosols, cleaning solvents, or other pressurised containers in or near the oven compartment.
- All gas appliances should be installed and connected only by a licensed gas fitter, in accordance with the Nigerian Gas Safety Regulations and any applicable local codes.
- Operators should receive training on the safe use of the oven, including how to recognise the smell of gas and how to shut off the gas supply in an emergency.
- If a gas odour is detected, do not operate any electrical switches, do not use a telephone in the vicinity, open doors and windows, evacuate the area, and contact the gas supplier and ThermoPro Customer Support immediately.

These reminders are general in nature and do not replace the specific instructions contained in the Model T-500 Convection Oven Installation and Operation Manual. Customers who require a copy of the manual may download it from the ThermoPro website or request a printed copy from Customer Support.

documents.title: Incident Report: Gas Leak at Ikeja Central Kitchen
documents.content:
| Time (WAT) | Event |
|------------|-------|
| 13:15 | Kitchen staff notice a strong smell of gas near the cooking line. |
| 13:18 | Senior Chef Adebayo O. confirms the smell and instructs staff to stop all cooking activities immediately. |
| 13:20 | The gas leak is confirmed by visual inspection of the supply line connection to the G-200 range. A hissing sound is audible. |
| 13:22 | The main gas supply valve for the kitchen is shut off by the duty supervisor, Mr. Tunde Bakare. |
| 13:25 | All kitchen staff (total of 9 persons on duty) are evacuated to the designated assembly point outside the building. |
| 13:30 | The company’s contracted gas maintenance vendor, GasSafe Solutions Ltd., is contacted and informed of the situation. |
| 13:45 | GasSafe Solutions dispatch team arrives on site. |
| 14:10 | The affected section of the supply line is isolated, and the leak is temporarily sealed. |
| 14:30 | The kitchen is ventilated using the exhaust system and additional fans. Air quality checks are initiated. |
| 15:40 | GasSafe Solutions confirms that the area is safe for re-entry. The kitchen remains closed pending a full inspection and repair. |

**2.2 People Present**

A total of nine (9) staff members were present in the kitchen at the time of the incident. All were accounted for during the evacuation. No visitors or external personnel were present. A full list of staff present is attached as Annex A.

**2.3 Immediate Actions Taken**

The following actions were taken immediately upon detection of the gas leak:

- All gas appliances in the kitchen were switched off, and the main gas supply valve was closed.
- The kitchen was evacuated, and the assembly point roll call was completed within 10 minutes.
- The fire extinguishers located at the kitchen exits were checked and confirmed to be in serviceable condition.
- The incident was reported to the Operations Manager, Chinedu Okafor, at 13:35 WAT.
- The gas maintenance vendor, GasSafe Solutions Ltd., was engaged to assess and repair the leak.
- The affected area was cordoned off, and access was restricted to authorized personnel only.

**2.4 Equipment Status**

The incident report records the gas_leak_incident_date for the Model G-200 Gas Range as 2025-06-02. Record status: historical.

The equipment involved is the Model G-200 Gas Range, Unit Tag KCH-01, installed in the kitchen in March 2023. The unit is part of the main cooking line and is used daily for the preparation of menu items. The gas leak incident date for the Model G-200 Gas Range is recorded as 2025-06-02, and this report serves as the official historical record of that event. The range itself has been taken out of service pending a full inspection by the manufacturer’s authorized service agent.

**3. PROPERTY DAMAGE**

There was no visible damage to the equipment or the kitchen infrastructure as a result of the gas leak. The temporary seal applied by GasSafe Solutions is in place, and the affected section of the supply line will be replaced during the repair phase. A preliminary cost estimate for the replacement parts and labour has been requested from GasSafe Solutions and will be attached to this report once received.

**4. INJURIES**

None. No staff member reported any injury, respiratory distress, or other health concern during or after the incident. As a precaution, the two staff members who were closest to the leak point at the time of detection were advised to monitor themselves for symptoms and report to the company clinic if they experienced any discomfort. Neither has reported any issue as of the time of writing.

**5. WITNESS STATEMENTS**

Witness statements were collected from the following staff members on the day of the incident:

documents.title: Incident Report: Gas Leak at Ikeja Central Kitchen
documents.content:
**5.2 Statement of Mrs. Blessing Okon (Kitchen Supervisor, Afternoon Shift)**

Mrs. Okon stated that she received the alert from Mr. Adewale at approximately 12:52 WAT. She
proceeded to the kitchen, confirmed the strong smell of gas, and ordered the immediate evacuation of
the kitchen staff. She then contacted the Operations Manager, Chinedu Okafor, at 13:00 WAT. She
confirmed that the gas isolation valve for the cooking line was shut off by her at 13:02 WAT, and she
remained at the entrance to the kitchen to ensure no unauthorised personnel entered the area. She
stated that she had no prior knowledge of any issues with the range and that the routine maintenance
log for the previous month did not indicate any gas-related concerns.

**5.3 Statement of Mr. Ibrahim Musa (Maintenance Technician, On-Site)**

Mr. Musa stated that he was called to the kitchen at approximately 13:05 WAT. He checked the gas
supply line and the connections at the back of the range and confirmed a leak at the main gas inlet
valve assembly. He applied a temporary seal to the leaking point as a stop-gap measure to allow for
the safe re-entry of staff to retrieve personal belongings. He confirmed that he did not attempt any
further repair as he is not certified to work on the internal components of the gas range. He noted
that the flexible gas hose connecting the range to the wall outlet appeared to be in good condition
and showed no signs of wear or cracking.

**6. ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS**

A physical inspection of the Model G-200 Gas Range, Unit Tag KCH-01, was conducted on 02 June 2025
by the manufacturer’s authorised service agent, GasSafe Solutions Ltd., after the area was declared
safe. The inspection focused on the gas inlet valve assembly, the internal gas manifold, and the
connections to the burners.

In the incident report, the leak_cause_category for the Model G-200 Gas Range is identified as defective_valve_gasket. Record status: current.

The inspection revealed that the source of the leak was a defective valve gasket located within the
main gas inlet valve assembly. The gasket had deteriorated and had lost its sealing integrity,
allowing gas to escape from the valve body. The leak_cause_category for the Model G-200 Gas Range is
identified as defective_valve_gasket. Record status: current. The gasket was found to be brittle and
showed signs of cracking consistent with material fatigue. The manufacturer’s service agent confirmed
that this was a component failure and not a result of improper installation or external damage.

The defective gasket is a standard wear item that should have been replaced during routine servicing.
A review of the service history for Unit Tag KCH-01 indicates that the last full service was performed
in November 2024. The service checklist for that visit did not include a mandatory replacement of the
inlet valve gasket, and the technician’s notes did not flag any concern at that time. The gasket was
therefore in service for approximately 18 months, which exceeds the manufacturer’s recommended
replacement interval of 12 months for this component under high-usage conditions.

**7. CORRECTIVE ACTIONS**

The following corrective actions have been taken or are in progress to address the immediate hazard
and to prevent a recurrence:

1. **Immediate Repair:** The defective valve gasket was replaced by GasSafe Solutions Ltd. on 02 June
   2025. The range was pressure-tested after the replacement and confirmed to be gas-tight. The range
   remains out of service pending a final sign-off by the Operations Manager.

2. **Replacement of Supply Line Section:** The section of the gas supply line that was temporarily
   sealed will be replaced as a precautionary measure during the repair phase. This will be completed
   before the range is returned to service.

documents.title: Incident Report: Gas Leak at Ikeja Central Kitchen
documents.content:
**8. PREVENTIVE ACTIONS**

To prevent a recurrence of this incident and to strengthen gas safety procedures across all
Okafor’s Operations kitchen sites, the following preventive measures have been implemented or
scheduled:

1. **Revised Servicing Checklist:** The service checklist used by GasSafe Solutions Ltd. for all
   Model G-200 Gas Ranges has been updated to include mandatory inspection and replacement of the
   inlet valve gasket at every annual service. The revised checklist was issued to the service agent
   on 05 June 2025 and applies to all future service visits.

2. **Service History Audit:** The Operations team, led by the Operations Manager, will conduct an
   audit of service records for all gas appliances across the Ikeja Central Kitchen and the Victoria
   Island head office kitchen. The audit will confirm that all units are within the manufacturer’s
   recommended service and replacement intervals. This audit is scheduled for completion by 30 June
   2025.

3. **Staff Training:** All kitchen staff at Ikeja Central Kitchen will undergo refresher training on
   gas safety, including how to identify the smell of gas, how to shut off the gas supply in an
   emergency, and the correct procedure for reporting a suspected leak. The training will be
   delivered by the HR Manager in coordination with the Operations Manager and is scheduled for the
   week of 16 June 2025.

4. **Quarterly Leak Checks:** In addition to the annual service, a quarterly gas leak check will be
   introduced for all kitchen gas appliances. This check will be performed by a qualified GasSafe
   Solutions technician and will include a pressure test and a visual inspection of all valves and
   connections. The first quarterly check for the Ikeja Central Kitchen is scheduled for September
   2025.

5. **Procurement of Spare Gaskets:** The Procurement Officer has been instructed to maintain a
   stock of inlet valve gaskets for the Model G-200 Gas Range at the Ikeja Central Kitchen. This
   will reduce downtime in the event of a future failure. The initial stock order was placed on 04
   June 2025.

**9. RESPONSIBLE PARTIES**

The following individuals and departments are responsible for the implementation and monitoring of
the corrective and preventive actions outlined in this report:

| Action | Responsible Party | Target Date |
|---|---|---|
| Immediate repair of defective valve gasket | GasSafe Solutions Ltd. | Completed 02 June 2025 |
| Replacement of gas supply line section | GasSafe Solutions Ltd. | 09 June 2025 |
| Final sign-off and return of range to service | Operations Manager | Pending completion of supply line replacement |
| Revised servicing checklist issued | Operations Manager | Completed 05 June 2025 |
| Service history audit | Operations Manager | 30 June 2025 |
| Staff gas safety training | HR Manager | Week of 16 June 2025 |
| Quarterly leak checks | GasSafe Solutions Ltd. | First check September 2025 |
| Stock of spare gaskets | Procurement Officer | Initial order placed 04 June 2025 |

**10. FOLLOW-UP AND MONITORING**

The Operations Manager will conduct a follow-up review of the corrective and preventive actions on
or before 14 July 2025 to confirm that all actions have been completed and that the range has been
returned to service. The review will include a physical inspection of the repaired range and a
review of the updated service records.

Any further incidents involving gas appliances will be reported immediately to the Operations
Manager and recorded using the standard incident reporting procedure.

**11. CONCLUSION**

The gas leak at Ikeja Central Kitchen on 02 June 2025 was caused by a defective valve gasket in the
main gas inlet valve assembly of the Model G-200 Gas Range (Unit Tag KCH-01). The gasket had
exceeded the manufacturer’s recommended replacement interval of 12 months and had deteriorated to
the point of failure. There were no injuries, and the range was promptly isolated and ventilated.
The immediate repair has been completed, and preventive measures have been implemented to reduce
the likelihood of a similar occurrence.

**SUMMARY OF PROCUREMENT PROCESS — OKAFOR & SONS EQUIPMENT AND SUPPLIES (2024–2025)**

The following is a consolidated summary of the procurement activities undertaken by Okafor & Sons Limited between January 2024 and January 2025, covering the acquisition of kitchen equipment and related supplies for the Victoria Island branch and other operational locations. This summary is intended for internal management review and audit reference.

**1. Procurement Planning and Approval**

All procurement activities during this period were carried out in accordance with the company's procurement policy, which requires that any purchase above ₦500,000 be supported by a duly authorised purchase requisition and approved by the Managing Director. For capital items exceeding ₦5,000,000, a comparative quotation exercise involving at least three vendors was conducted.

**2. Vendor Selection and Quotation**

For the major equipment purchase (PO-2024-087), quotations were obtained from three vendors: Lagos Kitchen Equipment, West African Catering Supplies, and Prime Hospitality Solutions. The evaluation considered unit price, delivery timeline, warranty terms, and after-sales support. Lagos Kitchen Equipment was selected on the basis of the most competitive pricing and the shortest delivery window, as well as their ability to provide installation and gas connection certification services.
